pharisees.name: Pharisees (Perushim)
theology: Belief in Oral Torah alongside Written Torah
Angels and divine providence balanced with human free will
Purity laws extended to the domestic table
pharisees.successor: Rabbinic Judaism is the direct historical heir to the Pharisaic movement

sadducees.name: Sadducees (Tzedokim)
sadducees.social_base: Aristocratic high priesthood, wealthy Temple elite
theology: Rejection of the Oral Torah; adherence strictly to the written Pentateuch
Denial of bodily resurrection of the dead
Denial of angels and deterministic fate
Strict literalism regarding purity and Temple penalties
sadducees.disappearance: Disappeared following the destruction of the Second Temple in 70 CE when the priestly sacrificial apparatus ceased

essenes.name: Essenes (likely Qumran Community / Yahad)
theology: Rejection of the Jerusalem Temple priesthood as corrupt and illegitimate
Apocalyptic dualism: Sons of Light vs Sons of Darkness
Extensive ritual immersion, communal property, strict hierarchy

zealots_sicarii.name: Zealots (Kannaim) & Sicarii
zealots_sicarii.social_base: Militant nationalists founded by Judas the Galilean (6 CE)
theology: No ruler but God (rejection of Roman tax as idolatry)
Active military revolt to force divine intervention
Led defense of Jerusalem (70 CE) and Masada (73 CE)

destruction_70_ce.event: Siege and Destruction of Second Temple by Roman General Titus in 70 CE
consequences: End of animal sacrifices and hereditary Aaronic priestly hegemony
Yochanan ben Zakkai established the Academy at Yavneh (Kerem Be-Yavneh)
Transformation from a localized Temple-sacrificial cult to a portable text-, prayer-, and halakha-based global religious system
